candidate.summary: Suflyor is a free, open-source teleprompter for Android that follows your voice using on-device streaming recognition, then floats its text over the camera app so Instagram, TikTok or the stock camera keeps recording with its own audio. features: On-device streaming speech recognition for English, Russian and Turkish, with ten more languages as one-time speech packs.
Re-reading a line returns the script to it after about two words, while pauses and off-script talk leave the text where it is.
Lock mode passes touches straight through the overlay to the camera app's own buttons, and landscape mode turns the text even when the camera stays portrait.

candidate.insight: Shipping a voice-following prompter with no INTERNET permission is a strong design statement, because the recognition could so easily have been a cloud call. F7 respects the trade: the app pins its own speech models at build time and lets you verify the permission list yourself.

candidate.summary: CalibRaw is a free, open-source RAW photo editor for Linux, Android, Windows and macOS, written in Rust with a wgpu and egui interface that runs image processing in compute shaders. Its AI tools, including masks, AI Remove and denoise, all run offline on your own machine.

The Android ARM64 app uses the same engine and .calibraw sidecars as the desktop build, with touch layouts and MediaStore exporting.
Edit Replay exports a 30 FPS MP4 of an edit step by step, while tiled export and a command-line tool render large RAW batches.
candidate.insight: An ARM64 Android build that opens the same sidecar files as the desktop app is the cross-platform trick F7 keeps chasing: one Rust engine and one project format, with touch layouts instead of a watered-down mobile core.
